one_line: Gurjara-Pratihara emperor who secured Kannauj and rebuilt the Somanatha shrine on the western frontier.

appearance.face: oval face with strong jaw, wheatish North Indian complexion, straight nose, sharp dark eyes with thick brows, neatly trimmed mustache and short beard framing the chin, default expression calm and commanding with a hint of stern focus
appearance.hair: thick black hair pulled back into a high warrior’s topknot, sides smoothly drawn back, wrapped at the base with a narrow crimson cloth band; a simple gold circlet with a central teardrop motif sits low on the forehead like a modest royal headband
appearance.costume: era-accurate early medieval North Indian royal warrior attire: a fitted, long-sleeved tunic (angarkha-style) in deep maroon cotton reaching mid-thigh, tied slightly off-center with gold edging at the neckline and cuffs; over this, a sleeveless quilted vest in muted bronze-brown suggesting light padded armor; lower body in tightly wrapped cream-coloured dhoti with a broad border in dull gold and indigo forming soft, dynamic folds down to the ankles; a rich saffron-orange cotton sash (patka) wrapped around the waist and knotted at the left hip, its ends hanging with subtle geometric block-print motifs in red; a second, lighter shawl in pale grey-blue draped from the left shoulder across the chest and back, evoking a pilgrim-king on campaign; simple leather bracers on forearms and strapped sandals in dark brown leather; jewellery restrained but regal—medium gold hoop earrings, a short gold necklace with small bead-like elements, and a single gold armlet on the right biceps shaped like a coiled vine
appearance.signature: a long, slightly curved steel sword with a simple iron crossguard and a dark brown leather-wrapped hilt, carried in a plain brown scabbard with minimal brass fittings, worn at his left hip and often held in his right hand with the blade angled downward in a ready but controlled stance

ref_desc: Nagabhata II is a wheatish-complexioned, mustached and short-bearded Gurjara-Pratihara emperor with a black topknot and gold circlet, wearing a maroon tunic, bronze-brown vest, cream dhoti, saffron sash, grey-blue shawl and carrying a curved steel sword at his left hip.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character of Nagabhata II as a dignified early medieval Gurjara-Pratihara emperor on campaign: wheatish complexion, oval face, strong jaw, sharp dark eyes, thick brows, neatly trimmed mustache and small chin beard, black hair pulled into a high warrior’s topknot wrapped with a crimson cloth band, and a simple gold circlet with a central teardrop motif on his forehead. Show him in a deep maroon, long-sleeved angarkha-style tunic with gold edging, over which sits a sleeveless quilted vest in muted bronze-brown suggesting light armor. His lower garment is a cream dhoti with a broad dull-gold and indigo border, tightly wrapped with flowing folds to the ankles, tied with a rich saffron-orange sash at the waist, ends hanging with subtle red geometric motifs. Add a pale grey-blue shawl draped from left shoulder across chest and back, simple leather bracers on his forearms, dark brown strapped sandals, and restrained royal jewellery: gold hoop earrings, a short gold bead-like necklace, and a single gold armlet on his right biceps. At his left hip, show a long, slightly curved steel sword in a plain brown scabbard with minimal brass fittings, and in his right hand he lightly holds the hilt, blade angled down in a controlled, ready stance. Use deep maroon, saffron orange, cream, bronze-brown and indigo as dominant colours, with the overall pose projecting calm, commanding authority suitable for a king securing Kannauj and restoring frontier temples.
